description: A creeping evergreen dwarf shrub 5-25 cm tall that mats the heath, the boulders and the birch-wood floor, with tiny glossy, rolled, needle-like leaves crowded on trailing red-brown stems. Its shiny black berries ripen in August and stay on through the winter, food for ptarmigan, thrushes, ravens and foxes.

season_notes.winter: Dark olive to brownish, the old black berries still on the mats where the snow blows off.
season_notes.spring: Tiny purple-red flowers in May and June, easily missed.
season_notes.summer: Fresh shoots; green berries turning glossy black from August.
season_notes.fall: Ripe berries everywhere on the heath; birds and foxes eat them, and people pick them.

range.where: circumboreal and arctic-alpine; on Moskenesoya from the shore heath to the summit fell-field, and as the ground layer of the birch woods

notes: Grown from pink mountain heather (Phyllodoce empetriformis, named for its crowberry-like leaves), the library's Ericaceae with needle-like rolled leaves, as a flatter, wider mat (crown radius 1.7 of the height). COMPROMISES: the plant is a trailing, rooting mat; the generator grows a separate dome per plant from upright stems splayed from one base, so a carpet of crowberry is many low domes (a ground-layer or shrubfield form would suit it better); the revolute needle leaves are 5 mm 'lanceolate' leaves; the berries are single black 'bud' berries kept on from August to May. Heights, colours, phenology and the animals are the drafter's knowledge (no source read beyond the GBIF name check). The raven is in the animal library; the ptarmigan, fieldfare and red fox are GBIF ids not yet there. Lofoten's calendar: polar night in December and early January, birch bare from about October to the end of May, leaf-out in late May and June, autumn yellow in September; the climate is oceanic, winters mild for the latitude, the treeline low (a few hundred metres) under salt wind.
